title: Baselines on the benchmark, with the gate written first
request: Write the thresholds of the AND gate before any run, then run the standard plan, the audit reference, a prompted base model and the current agent on the sealed set with identical tools and budgets, and give a result per policy and family with intervals, every failure kept, and the gate's verdict as evidence about these policies on these cases, never as a production claim. The owner said to do everything that does not need other people.
spec: Gate thresholds written before any run (for example no unsafe move; leaks kept out on at least 90% of leak cases with the lower 95% bound above 80%; false alarms on at most 10% of controls); the four policies on the sealed set; results per policy and family with intervals; the verdict stated as evidence, never as a production claim.
plan: Write gate_v1 (dclab_rnd/agent_eval/gate.py) from the package text and docs/SYSTEM_EVALUATION.md, with tests that every criterion can fail alone and that missing numbers fail; commit it (48acdb4) before any new run on the sealed set.

Write baselines.py: a prompted base model that sees only each column's name, kind, missing share and distinct count plus the prediction moment, and sets its solution through the validator; register its prompt (base_audit.md) and store its fingerprint.
Run the base model on the sealed 70 cases with a cap (BEN-003), then the current agent, the intern on gpt-6-luna with its tools and 16 steps (BEN-004).
Build the gate report over all policies (BEN-005) after the reviewer's findings were fixed.
Run make check-all and commit with the kits and A5.1.

decisions.decision: The gate is committed before the base-model and agent runs, and a threshold moves only as a new gate version.
decisions.why: A gate chosen after the numbers are seen can be fitted to them.

decisions.decision: The scripted policies' sealed numbers (BEN-002), recorded earlier, are judged by the gate too, with the order stated.
decisions.why: Their numbers were known when the gate was written; the thresholds come from the package text, not from them, and a test and the report say so.

decisions.decision: The gate also fails a policy when any trap family of four or more leak cases is below 50%.
decisions.why: An aggregate rate can hide a family the policy never catches.

decisions.decision: The base model sees names and summaries only, never values, audit flags, target candidates or labels.
decisions.why: It is a baseline for judgment from the schema; anything more would leak the answer or test a different policy.

change: New dclab_rnd/agent_eval/gate.py (gate_v1 thresholds and verdict), baselines.py (the prompted base-model policy, caps checked before each request, failures kept, build_report over all policies), prompts/base_audit.md, live.py --split, tests/test_gate.py and tests/test_baselines.py, results BEN-003, BEN-004 and BEN-005.

findings.defect: The report did not check its inputs, so a dev or partial result could be judged as the sealed test gate.
findings.scenario: Passing a dev base-model file (split dev, 38 cases) produced a 'sealed test' verdict, because each policy's expected total was the file's own case count and the report wrote split test and sealed true regardless; a dev agent file crashed with a bare KeyError.
findings.cause: The expected total was circular and the split was never compared with the benchmark.
findings.fix: Require every input's split to be test and its case ids and fingerprints to equal the sealed set; the expected total is the sealed set's size (times repeats for the agent).
findings.impact: A dev-set file, or a run on a subset, could be published as the sealed test verdict, with 'every case ran' passing by circular counting; the one gate meant to be judged once, on the sealed set, could have been judged on the wrong evidence.

findings.defect: False alarms were counted over all cases with a clean column, not over controls as the package text says.
findings.scenario: On the 32 pure control cases the base model has 3 false alarms against 6 of 70 as gated, and the audit 13 of 32 against 18 of 70; a policy could pass as implemented and fail the literal text.
findings.cause: The gate used the benchmark's existing false-alarm count.
findings.fix: The gate keeps its definition (stated in the 14.5 text and the limitations), and the report gives both rates: over the 70 cases and over the 32 pure controls.
findings.impact: A policy could pass the gate as built while failing the gate as written in the playbook, because false alarms were averaged over cases where most columns are clean; the denominator decides whether the agent's false-alarm rate looks acceptable.
alternatives: Gate on the pure controls only, as a new gate version: set aside because the gate was fixed before the runs; the definition stays and both rates are reported.

findings.defect: The base model's prompt names the benchmark's trap families almost one for one.
findings.scenario: The prompt mentions a copy of the target in another unit, a sum or difference, a value that exists only when the outcome happened and a harmless name that sounds like an outcome, so it is a hinted baseline, not a plain prompted model; the playbook asks for identical tools and budgets, but the base model has no tools and the agent has 16 steps.
findings.cause: The prompt was written with the families in mind.
findings.fix: Stated in the result's limitations and the playbook row as a hinted baseline; the differences in tools and steps are disclosed.
findings.impact: The prompted base model looked closer to the agent than a plain model would, because its prompt hinted at the very trap families being scored; a comparison of the two would credit the base model with knowledge the prompt handed it.
findings.open: The base model also has no tools while the agent has 16 steps, so the two are not compared on identical tools and budgets as the package asked.

measurements.name: gate_v1 on the sealed 70 cases (BEN-005)
measurements.gate: Leaks kept out on at least 90% of leak cases with the 95% lower bound at least 80%; false alarms at most 10%; valid moves 1.0; every cited record real; every case scored; no trap family of four or more leak cases below 50%. All must hold.
measurements.result: No policy passes. Leaks kept out of 38 / false alarms of 70 (of the 32 pure controls): standard plan 7 (9–33%) / 12 (7); audit rules 28 (58–85%) / 18 (13); bad policy 0 / 0 with valid moves 0.75; prompted base model 33 (73–94%) / 6 (3); the agent 35 (79–97%) / 26 (21), valid moves and citations 1.0. The agent forbids clean columns on 37% of cases (for example a real wine feature), and 53 of its 70 runs ended on the step budget.
measurements.next: The agent's over-forbidding of clean columns is the next engineering target; the base model is closest on false alarms and short on leaks. Labels are the author's until 14.4; one repeat per case.
measurements.against_gate: No policy meets every condition. The agent kept 35 of 38 leaks out, but its interval of 79–97% starts below the required lower bound of 80%, and its 26 false alarms in 70 are well over the 10% allowed; its valid moves and citations at 1.0 pass. The prompted base model kept 33 of 38 out, short of 90%, with an interval of 73–94% that also starts below 80%, though its 6 false alarms in 70 stay within 10%. The audit rules (28, 58–85%, with 18 false alarms) and the standard plan (7, 9–33%, with 12) fail on leaks and on false alarms. The bad policy kept 0 out and its valid moves of 0.75 fall short of 1.0.
limits: The labels are the author's until the expert review; every rate depends on them.
The base model's prompt hints at the trap families, and it has no tools while the agent has steps, so the two are not compared on equal terms.
53 of the agent's 70 runs ended on the step budget, so its result is for unfinished runs.
The sealed set has now been scored by every policy; any change tuned after reading these numbers needs a new sealed version to be tested fairly.

outcome: Done (48acdb4 for the gate, c291a1b for the runs and the report): no policy passes gate_v1 on the sealed set; the agent keeps the most leaks out and fails on false alarms. The verdict is evidence about these policies on these cases, not a production claim.
lessons: Commit the gate before the run, and let the report refuse any input that is not exactly the sealed set.
A gate's denominator is part of the gate: state it and report the literal reading beside it.
A baseline prompt that names the trap families is a hinted baseline; say so, or it flatters the comparison.
An agent that catches the most leaks by forbidding clean columns has not passed; false alarms are part of safety for a data scientist.
risks: A gate written after seeing the numbers can be bent to the result; the thresholds must be committed before any run.
The report must check that its inputs are the sealed test split, complete, or it can judge the wrong evidence.
A false-alarm rate depends on its denominator; the gate's definition and the playbook text must say the same thing.
A prompted baseline can be hinted toward the benchmark's families, inflating it next to the agent.
A model's run that ends on the step budget is scored as if finished unless that is reported alongside.
